summary: WebSocket/control-plane sessions misattributed to wrong pod after edge NAT port remap causing mid-stream 401s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent streaming failures (WebSocket upgrade and gRPC-over-websocket) on Private deployment. Connections initially succeed but subsequent requests from the same client are routed to a different serving pod, resulting in KV cache misses, token validation failures, and immediate disconnects.

Impact:
- Affects NovaAI prod cluster in eu-west-1. ~8% of streaming sessions observed disconnecting within 30s over the last 24h. User-visible: aborted responses, auth errors (401) mid-stream.
- Blockers for production rollouts; customer stalled new model rollout until root cause identified.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed edge NAT + on-prem k8s).
- Customer uses k8s hostPort-based sidecar for ingress to serving nodes. Edge device: Cisco ASR virtualized firewall performing NAT44 with port reuse and connection tracking disabled for UDP flows.
- Redwood control-plane endpoints reachable via VPCE to us-east; serving nodes ingress via customer's public egress NAT.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Client opens a streaming session to the hosted endpoint (ws://...). 2. Server upgrades and handshake completes; tokens validated. 3. Client sends several messages; after ~20-90s, client sends keepalive and new request and receives 401 / immediate RST.
4. On customer side, a new packet flow is observed with same source IP but different source port mapping, and the edge NAT forwards it to a different backend pod.

Observed logs and telemetry:
- Control plane logs show session_id X mapped to pod A at t=12:03:14; at t=12:03:45 an auth token validated against session metadata pointing at pod B -> 401.
- SRE packet-capture (pcap) from customer edge shows source port reallocation for TCP flow after 18s; netstat on pod shows previous connection still ESTABLISHED.
- No TLS handshake error; TLS session continued but application-layer routing changed.

Hypothesis:
- Customer edge NAT is performing aggressive source-port recycling for long-lived connections when conntrack table is near threshold; combined with k8s hostPort forwarding rules (iptables MARK-based routing), the NAT port remap causes packets to be routed to the wrong node/pod. This leads to session misattribution in the serving runtime (KV cache tied to pod-level memory) and token state mismatch.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Requested customer to increase conntrack max and reduce NAT port reuse rate; they increased net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established and nf_conntrack_max temporarily. This reduced error rate to ~0.5% within 2 hours.
- As a short-term workaround, enabled sticky routing on the customer edge using conntrack-based NAT with session-affinity (src-ip+src-port+dst-port) and configured host-level NAT hairpin avoidance on nodes.

Investigation notes:
- Replayed traffic in staging with a lab edge device reproduces port reuse when conntrack limit exceeded. When conntrack entries are dropped, NAT assigns new ephemeral ports causing in-flight TCP packets to be misdelivered.
- Serving runtime does not currently verify per-packet connection 4-tuple beyond the socket-level accept path; when packets arrive at different pod, the runtime treats as a new session and rejects those frames.
- SRE engineering confirmed a potential enhancement: include session tokens in a short-lived distributed lookup (consistent hash fallback) to allow session rehydration when routing flips; tracked as a follow-up engineering task.

Next steps:
- SRE to provide a recommended conntrack/sysctl profile for private deployments (document + runbook).
- Engineering to assess feasibility of session rehydration fallback in runtime (tracked in GH PR above).
- Customer to keep increased conntrack limits; monitor for 72 hours and confirm stability.

Resolution notes:
- Temporary mitigation (conntrack increase + session-affinity) applied by customer reduced error rate to acceptable level. Engineering follow-up required for a durable server-side fallback. Customer agreed to re-open if errors reoccur.
resolution: Workaround implemented by customer: increased conntrack table and enabled NAT session-affinity on edge. Reduced errors from ~8% to ~0.5%. Engineering follow-up required for session rehydration support in serving runtime (tracked in PR above).
comments: Customer (NovaAI) initial report: 'Streaming sessions drop mid-way; tokens rejected although we didn't rotate keys. Occurs across multiple regions but most in eu-west.' — 2026-03-01 08:15 UTC
Support triage: Confirmed pattern of mid-stream 401s and disconnects. Requested packet captures and netstat from customer. Assigned to networking SRE. — Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-01 09:02

SRE analysis: PCAP shows TCP source port remap while original connection still ESTABLISHED. Hypothesis: conntrack exhaustion + NAT port reuse. Asking customer to raise conntrack limits and retest. — Diego Ramos (SRE) 2026-03-01 11:40

Customer action: Increased nf_conntrack_max to 1.5M and tcp_timeout_established to 86400s; observed immediate reduction in errors. Also applied source NAT sticky mapping. — NovaAI network team 2026-03-01 15:20

Engineering note: Runtime enhancement planned: short-lived distributed session index to allow rehydrate if routing flips. See GH PR linked. Prioritization TBR. — Priya Venkataraman (Runtime) 2026-03-03 10:05
